title: regional placement simulator and evacuation contract
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Build a simulator and a binding evacuation contract that lets Dedicated fleet owners specify placement constraints, measurable throughput guarantees, and predictable failover behavior across regions and zones while ensuring data residency controls are respected. The goal is a deterministic planner that can validate customer SLAs, surface policy conflicts, and produce safe evacuation plans and prewarm actions for autoscale events.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can ingest a customer placement policy document and output a timeline of requests routed across regions/zones with per-minute throughput and latency estimates
Evacuation contract generator produces a stepwise failover plan that includes capacity escrow, prewarm steps, and least-disruptive traffic shift with rollback points
Simulator flags policy violations where data residency or sovereignty constraints would be breached and outputs an alternative compliant plan
End-to-end test harness reproduces a 3-hour simulated regional outage with synthetic workloads and validates throughput guarantees within 95% of target under soft-failover and 90% under hard-failover
Runbook with operator playbook and automated run commands is checked into docs and referenced from the Dedicated Console
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Design a JSON placement policy schema (region preferences, zone affinity, residency locks, escalation order, throughput targets)
Phase 2: Implement planner/simulator that uses historical traffic percentiles and current capacity snapshots to compute feasible allocations
Phase 3: Integrate with Autoscaler to emit prewarm requests and capacity escrow ops during planned evacuations
Phase 4: Wire into Console to visualize simulated timelines and show policy conflicts
We will reuse the kernel-cost model from serving-runtime to estimate token-throughput per GPU slot and map to region capacity
decisions: Use a conservative throughput envelope (p90 token throughput) for guarantee calculations to avoid SLA breaches
Evacuation plans will prefer intra-region spillover before cross-region failover when residency allows
Introduce a residency-escrow token model: customers can reserve a small token pool for emergency cross-region execution subject to audit and TTL
Simulator output will include both optimistic and conservative scenarios to guide operator decisions
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Initial design doc shared to Confluence (link below). Collected feedback from PM and Security on residency-escrow proposal.
2025-02-20: PoC simulator can replay a 24h trace and generate zone allocations. Identified mismatch in kernel throughput assumptions for quantized models.
2025-02-27: Implemented policy validator that rejects configurations with circular failover references. Added unit tests for validator.
2025-03-03: Integrated Autoscaler stub to emit prewarm webhook. Simulated soft-failover and measured 12% higher tail latency for long-context workloads.
2025-03-05: Security reviewed residency-escrow flow; requested audit trail fields and KMS-backed tokens. Incorporating changes this sprint.
review_feedback: PM (Dana Cho): Ensure simulator exposes clear user-facing reasons when guarantees cannot be satisfied; add remediation suggestions
Design (Lena Morris): Visualization needs a timeline view with color-coded residency violations and an expandable step list
Security (Adrian McKay): Escrow tokens must be HSM/KMS-bound and TTL-limited; include immutable audit entries for any cross-region execution
SRE (Omar Khatri): Add a chaos test that flips zone affinity mid-simulate to validate graceful drain behavior and metrics retention
qa_plan: Create 3 synthetic tenant profiles (small, medium, enterprise) and assert throughput targets under normal, soft-failover, and hard-failover scenarios
Run nightly simulator tests against latest capacity snapshot; surface regressions in a CI dashboard
Manual DR drill between us-west and eu-west with SRE observing metrics and executing rollback steps
migration_plan: Phase A: Beta with a subset of Dedicated customers who opt into simulated SLAs
Phase B: Offer simulator in Console as a preview, allow customers to export evacuation contract for signing
Phase C: Enforce residency-escrow contracts for cross-region emergency execution for enterprise customers
